data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's own stated countercondition is decisive against its claim: 'If anthropogenic heat is a small fraction of the daytime storage, it cannot explain the full magnitude of the nocturnal gap.' Decades of urban energy-balance measurements confirm exactly that condition: anthropogenic heat flux is typically a minor term relative to daytime storage and net radiation, and nocturnal UHI persists strongly even in cities/seasons with minimal heating, traffic, or industry. By SRC_001's own falsification rule, that observation eliminates anthropogenic heat as the best single mechanism, yet the target still asserts it as dominant. The target also fails to distinguish the two parts of the question: it conflates 'why the city is warmer at night' with 'why the gap varies across cities,' and its cross-city proxy (population/energy) is empirically weak relative to geometry/sky-view as the actual modulator of nocturnal release.
